messages:
alex: Repro + perf regression when running paged-flash with interleaved KV + bf16. Dumped nsight timeline and kernel selection logs. @maria @tony can you take a look?

maria: Thanks. Can you paste the exact command and kernel log? small reproduction would help.

alex: Repro command I used:
```
RUNTIME_PROF=1 ./bench_attention --model=llama-7b --seq=2048 --batch=8 --kv-layout=interleaved --dtype=bf16 --kernel=paged-flash --kv-pad=0
```
Kernel selector output snippet:
```
[selector] model=llama-7b seq=2048 batch=8 dtype=bf16 hw=A100
[selector] candidates: paged_flash_coalesce, fused_flash, packed_flash
[selector] picked: paged_flash_coalesce (reason: fits page policy)
[perf] tokens/sec: 8,200 (expected ~12,000)
[prof] L2 miss rate=23.4%  warp_stalls=high  sm_occupancy=34%
```
Behavior: switching to packed layout or forcing fused-flash brings tokens/sec back to ~12k.

tony: Sounds like an alignment/stride issue. Interleaved layout changed per-key stride from 64->48 bytes after bf16 packing? If stride is not 64-aligned we get uncoalesced loads on page boundaries and the paged coalesce kernel loses vectorization.

maria: Do you have the buffer layout math? exact stride we observed?

alex: Yes — the per-kv entry size (k+v) after bf16 quantization ended up 48 bytes for our config: 16 (k) + 32 (v) due to packing + dropout meta. Page size in kernel is 256. 256 % 48 = 16 => misaligned across pages -> partial loads.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary run 2025-11-09T20:13 failed for paged_flash_coalesce on internal/llama-7b tests. Reverted canary.

sara: Quick mitigation: pad per-entry stride to nearest 64 bytes when dtype==bf16 or when using interleaved layout. That will keep page boundaries aligned and should restore coalesced loads. Example heuristic: kv_stride = align_up(kv_stride, 64).

alex: I ran a microbench with padding to 64 bytes:
```
--kv-pad=16 (adds 16 bytes per entry)
before: tokens/sec=8200
after:  tokens/sec=11950
nsight: L2 miss rate down to 7.1%  sm_occupancy=66%  warp_stalls=low
```

devon: Nice. We should also harden the kernel selector rather than rely on manual padding. Proposed rule: if layout==interleaved and dtype in {bf16, fp16} then prefer fused/paged variant only when kv_stride%64==0; otherwise fallback to packed kernel or inject padding. I'll open a small PR to implement.

maria: +1. Also add a unit microbench that asserts tokens/sec delta < 5% for canary baseline vs candidate on our regression harness (seq>=1024, batch>=8).

tony: One more nuance: some models have per-token extra metadata so stride can vary across models. Selector should compute expected stride from model config (embedding dim, kv-projection layout) at model load time. Add cache of that calc.

alex: Action plan: 1) devon to land kernel-selector guard (hotfix) 2) add kv-stride alignment calc in model onboarding 3) sara will add optional runtime pad flag default on for hosted canary 4) maria add microbench regression test. I'll file the ticket and attach nsight trace.

ci-bot: ticket-1234 created: "kv stride alignment -> paged-flash perf regression (bf16, interleaved)" assigned to devon.

devon: Taking ticket-1234. I'll run a matrix across seq {512,1024,2048} x batch {4,8,16} x dtype {bf16,fp16,fp32} and post a summary later today.

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
